walkthroughs.body_html:
Presenting Music — a core area of Music.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Presenting Music brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Presenting Music.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Whose 1953 Concentus Musicus Wien revived historically informed Baroque playing?
options: John Eliot Gardiner
Nikolaus Harnoncourt
Christopher Hogwood
Roger Norrington
Susan McClary
Christopher Small
Lawrence Kramer
Nicholas Cook

mcqs.q: How many semitones are in a perfect fifth?
options: 5 (counting letter-name positions).
Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.

mcqs.q: What is a tone row in serial music?
options: An ordered series of all 12 chromatic pitches, used as the basis of a piece.
Adjusting volume electronically.
Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.
A row of notes played together as a chord.

mcqs.q: What does modulation mean in music?
options: Adjusting volume electronically.
Changing from one key to another within a piece.
Any sequence of notes a composer chooses.
Changing tempo or dynamics.
